stem: An intern attends a dinner party and recognizes a resident colleague who works at the same hospital in another department.  Early in the evening, the intern notices that the resident is drinking a glass of wine while responding to what sounds like a routine medical call from the hospital.  The intern approaches the resident to say hello, and the resident says, "I'm on call but luckily it's been pretty slow--only a few more hours to go."  An hour later, the intern notes that the resident has finished 3 beers and is continuing to take calls from the hospital and give patient orders over the phone.  Which of the following is the most appropriate next step for the intern to take at this time?​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​​​​​‌​​​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌

options.label: A
options.text: Advise the resident to transfer remaining on-call responsibilities to another resident

options.label: B
options.text: Ask the resident to not drink any more alcohol until the on-call shift is over

options.label: C
options.text: Contact the resident's on-call supervisor immediately

options.label: D
options.text: Report the resident to the hospital's physician health program for alcohol use disorder

options.label: E
options.text: Report the resident to the state medical board if any signs of alcohol intoxication are observed

explanation:
Physicians have an ethical duty to report impaired colleagues in a timely and appropriate manner.  This intern is in the uncomfortable position of witnessing a colleague drink several alcoholic beverages (ie, 4 in 1 hr) while on duty, raising concern that the colleague has provided medical care while acutely intoxicated.  Although it is unclear whether the resident's drinking while on call reflects an isolated incident or a chronic condition (ie, alcohol use disorder), the intern is obligated to intervene immediately because patient safety is at risk.  Therefore, the intern should inform the colleague's on-call supervisor now so the current situation can be dealt with as quickly as possible.

Substance use disorders are common among physicians, as they are in the general population.  Signs of a chronic condition are frequently subtle and may include:

  • Increased irritability and aggressive outbursts

  • Increasingly disheveled appearance

  • Frequent absences or tardiness to appointments (eg, rounds, meetings)

When a physician is concerned about a colleague's possible impairment in a general, nonemergency sense (eg, noticing concerning signs rather than observing the colleague provide care while consuming alcohol), reporting the colleague to the physician health program (PHP) is appropriate.  PHPs are committees that assess physicians to determine whether substance use disorders and comorbid psychiatric or medical conditions are present; these committees also facilitate treatment.  PHP referral is typically anonymous and may eventually be needed for this resident if the behavior is part of a larger concerning pattern.  However, at this time, contacting the colleague's supervisor is more appropriate because of witnessed excessive alcohol consumption and concern for patient safety (Choice D).

(Choices A and B)  Relying on the resident to take action (eg, transfer duties, stop drinking) is inappropriate because the resident's judgment may be impaired from alcohol consumption.  Moreover, because medical care has already been provided (eg, telephone orders), the intern has a duty to report the situation now to avoid patient harm.

(Choice E)  In most cases, especially if the pattern or severity of impairment is uncertain, contacting the state licensing board would be inadequate.  The licensing board focuses primarily on disciplinary action (eg, license revocation); for this emergent scenario, contacting the resident's supervisor is the most appropriate action.

Educational objective:Physicians are ethically and legally obligated to report impaired colleagues in a timely manner.  Reporting protects patient safety and can help impaired physicians receive appropriate evaluation and treatment.​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​​​​​‌​​​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌
